3. Eventually, the borrower failed to repay the loan liability and in the circumstances, the Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 18 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet (the Adalat) for recovery of Tk. 1,36,10,008.45 by furnishing the schedule property along with other properties against the borrower and the writ petitioners. No notice/summons was served upon the writ petitioners and their brothers and as such, the writ petitioners had no knowledge about the said artha rin suit. It is further stated in the writ petition that writ respondent No. 7 Abdullah Al Harun who had no nexus with the aforementioned credit facility, filed an application on 29.04.2010 under section 57 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 (the Ain) praying to implead him in the suit as defendant No.10 stating that he is a cousin of defendant No.4(borrower) and thus wishes to be a party to the suit for purchasing schedule 1-3 property of the suit including present schedule property towards adjustment of the loan liability of the borrower writ respondent No. 4 as due to the Bank. On the same day, i.e. on 29.04.2010 the Bank (plaintiff in the suit), writ respondent Nos. 3, 4, 5 and 6 (defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the suit) and writ respondent No. 7 (intended defendant No.10) submitted a solenama in Artha Rin Suit No.18 of 2009 praying to dismiss the suit in terms of the said solenama, and that by the solenama schedule-3 property along with two other schedules of the borrower were transferred in favour of writ respondent No.7 (intended defendant No.10) determining the price at Tk. 3,50,00,000/-. 

 4. As per terms of the solenama, out of the said amount Tk. 1,09,00,000/-  was to be paid to the Bank and the remaining Tk. 2,41,00,000/- would be paid to the defendant No. 4 (borrower) and that the Adalat without impleading the writ respondent No. 7 in the suit, accepted the said solenama on examination of the Bank's representative, defendant No.4(borrower) and writ respondent No. 7 and, accordingly, the suit was dismissed by order dated 05.05.2010 in terms of the solenama against the defendant Nos. 1-4 and 10 and ex party against the remaining defendants and that the solenama was made part of the decree. Subsequently, by order dated 16.06.2010 the Adalat considered the application of writ respondent No. 7 for adding him as defendant No.10 in the suit and allowing the said application the Adalat directed to amend the plaint, suit register and the decree accordingly. In this backdrop, the writ petitioners have challenged the aforementioned judgement and decree dated 05.05.2010 accepting the solenama, and obtained the Rule. 

 5. Appearing in the Rule the writ respondent Bank has filed affidavit-in-opposition controverting the contents of the writ petition. This respondent also contended that the writ petitioners by entering into a tripartite agreement allowed the Bank to take over possession of the schedule property (shops) and also for disposal of the said shops in favour of any third party. Therefore, the writ petitioners cannot raise any objection to such solenama wherein the Bank is a party and that the writ petitioners are estopped from denying the right of the Bank in transferring the possession of the shops to any third party. It is also contended that section 45 of the Ain does not restrict the parties to the suit from entering into amicable settlement. 

 "That in case of default or failure of the 1st party to repay the dues of the 2nd party, the 2nd party is entitled to take over possession of the aforesaid shop premises along with stock-in-trade and to sell/transfer the same to any new party or parties either by private contract or in public auction for recovery of their dues and in such a case neither the party nor the 3rd party shall raise any objection to or create any obstruction to such steps of the 2nd party (Annexure-B) to the writ petition." It was further contended that when the suit was in progress, the borrower respondent took steps to compromise the matter with a view to sell the schedule property and to adjust the Bank dues, and the said proposal was approved by the Head Office of the Bank. This respondent paid the entire liability of the borrower by executing a solenama. Therefore, it cannot be said that this respondent is not related to the subject matter of the suit and that in spite of entering into the tripartite agreement, the writ petitioners neither appeared in the suit nor took any step to resolve the dispute. The Ain has provided settlement of dispute in several stages of the suit and thus having legal sanction, the writ respondents settled the matter under section 45 of the Ain. This writ respondent also contended that having tenancy agreement, writ petitioner No. 1 for himself as well as on behalf of other petitioners, executed a declaration allowing the tenant (borrower) to transfer possession of the shop premises. 

 9. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. A.M. Amin Uddin learned Senior Advocate on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the impugned judgement and order dated 06.8.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7347 of 2010 are bad in law and fact because the High Court Division based their findings on surmise, conjectures and extraneous circumstances for which the said findings are liable to he struck down. He further submitted that the High Court Division manifestly failed to appreciate that there having been specific remedy in Section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the present Rule in Writ Petition No.7347 of 2010 challenging the propriety of the ex parte decree is not maintainable. He submitted that the High Court Division failed to notice that writ respondent No.7 filed the application for addition of party and it was duly noted on record, but inadvertently the Adalat did not pass any order for adding this respondent as defendant in the suit though subsequently, in the order sheet as well as in the decree, this respondent has been shown as defendant No.10. Therefore, it was a bonafide omission of the Adalat in not passing any formal order impleading respondent No. 7 as defendant and subsequently it being noticed, the Adalat by order date 16.06.2010 passed necessary order impleading respondent No. 7 as defendant No. 10. Accordingly, the decree and the other orders were corrected. In view of the facts, there is no illegality in passing the judgement and decree on the basis of solenama as filed by writ respondents Nos. 3, 4 and 7 and the Bank. This position is supported by the decisions in the cases of M. Majid Vs. Iqbal Bahar Chowdhury and others reported in 5 BLC (AD) 7, Dwijindra Lal Nath Vs. Abu Zafar reported in 30 DLR (SC) 74. The restrictions for impleading a party in the artha rin suit provided in section 6(5) of the said Ain is applicable only at the time of filing of the suit, but during pendency of the suit, the said provision does not apply. He submitted that the High Court Division overlooked that by the tripartite agreement as well as the declaration executed by one of the writ petitioners, the writ petitioners empowered the borrower writ respondent No. 4 (tenant) to transfer the possessory right of the schedule property and that in view of the aforesaid tripartite agreement as well as the declaration, writ respondent No. 4 entered into the solenama. Therefore, the writ petitioners are not required to be party in the said solenama, inasmuch as empowering writ respondent No. 4 they have already consented to transfer the possessory right of the schedule property. In any view of the matter, the writ petitioners remain as owner of the property and they will be entitled to get the rent of the schedule property, inasmuch as by the solenama writ respondent No. 7 has only stepped in the shoes of writ respondent No.4. Therefore, the writ petitioners are not entitled to any equitable relief under this writ jurisdiction. He submitted that non-addition of writ respondent No.7 as defendant in the suit was a mere omission of the Adalat though it was on record that writ respondent No. 7 filed an application for addition of party and the Adalat has shown him as defendant in passing the judgement. Therefore, it indicates that the Adalat considered him as defendant and accordingly, accepted the solenama in passing the decree. Subsequently, on 16.06.2010 on the prayer of writ respondent No. 7, the Adalat added respondent No. 7 in the suit by amending the record as well as decree. He also submitted that the High Court Division failed to reflect upon the statements made in the affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf' of the writ respondent No. 7 controverting those made in the writ petition. He submitted that the writ petition having involved disputed questions of fact and the writ petitioner having alternative remedy and no locus standi to file the writ petition, it was not maintainable and, as such, the High Court Division ought to have discharged the Rule. He submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider the legal provisions involved in this case and the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division is neither proper nor in accordance with law, and is liable to be set aside. 

 14. The High Court Division next considered the terms of the solenama which were quoted as follows: 

 15. The High Court Division went on to observe that defendant Nos. 5 to 9, who were the writ petitioners (respondents herein) are neither party in nor authorised any party to execute the said solenama. The High Court Division concluded that writ respondent 7, who was added as defendant No. 10 in the suit in connivance with the bank took steps to grab the petitioners' property by practicing fraud upon the Court and obtained the compromise decree. 

 16. Finally, relying upon the case of Mir Motiur Ralunan Zihadi Versus Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and another reported in 15 BLT (AD) 267, the High Court Division observed that the defendants of the suit were not parties in the solenama though their property was included therein. 

 17. Having considered the facts of the case as discussed above, we are of the view that since the respondents were neither party to the solenama nor the decree was passed in their presence the same is not binding upon them.
